chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfa, from Ma'mar ibn Ata' ibn Washeeka who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
'The people will not be correct regarding divorce except by the sword, and if I were to rule over them, I would refer them in it to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.السيف: The sword — a metaphor for political authority and coercive enforcement; here signifying the Imamic governance needed to restore Quranic law
key_terms.الطلاق: Talaq (divorce) — the formal Islamic procedure for dissolving a marriage, governed by strict Quranic rules (Quran 2:229, 65:1)
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — an epithet of God used frequently in hadith literature
key_terms.كتاب الله: The Book of God — the Quran, the foundational legal source for Islamic family law

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about divorce and the Book of God?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS), the fifth Imam, declared that the Muslim community had deviated so far from the correct rules of divorce (talaq) established in the Quran that only the authority of the sword — i.e., legitimate Imamic governance — could bring them back to compliance. Speaking hypothetically, the Imam expressed that if he held political authority, he would enforce the Quranic rules of divorce rather than the corrupt practices prevalent among the people. This hadith reflects the Imam's critique of the jurisprudential deviations of his era, where customary or politically convenient divorce practices had displaced the strict Quranic commands.
word_analysis: I were to rule over them

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Huzeyfa, from Ma’mar Bin Ata’a Bin Washeyka who said, 
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘The people would not be correct regarding the divorce except by the sword, and if I<sup>asws</sup> were to rule over them, I<sup>asws</sup> would refer them in it to the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 1. Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Hudhayfah, from Mu’ammar ibn (‘Ata’ ibn) Washik who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

People do not behave properly in matters of divorce without the sword. If you govern them, you can return them to the book of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’ He (the narrator) has said that al-Mithamiy from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from his narrators narrated guessing that this Hadith is from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam .’”
